_comment:
Byte-exact vectors for SimFW's per-command-group COMMAND PAYLOADS (docs/PROTOCOL.md sections 4/5) -- the layer *inside* a benchproto DATA frame's payload, distinct from firmware/CommonFW/test/vectors/benchproto_frame_vectors.json which only covers the frame envelope (header/CRC/reliability). Same convention as that manifest: request payload is [cmd_id, args...], reply payload is [status, fields...] (PROTOCOL.md sec 2), multi-byte fields are little-endian (BENCHPROTO.md sec 3), and every vector here is hand-derived from PROTOCOL.md's documented wire layout using a standalone struct.pack computation (see the gap-closure task report for the exact script) -- NOT generated by calling either tools/PcTools/src/kilnsim/payloads.py or firmware/SimFW/src/tasks/cmd_task.c, so a bug shared between those two production implementations would still show up as a mismatch against this manifest. Two independent consumers check every vector below: tools/PcTools/tests/test_kilnsim_cmd_payload_vectors.py (calls the real payloads.py encode_request()/decode_reply()) and firmware/SimFW/test/test_cmd_payload_vectors.c (a byte-for-byte mirror of cmd_task.c's arg_reader_t/reply_writer_t helpers and each covered handler's field sequence, following test_cmd_task_gap_closure.c's existing precedent for testing cmd_task.c's pure wire-layout logic without pulling in its FreeRTOS/sim_engine/i2c_owner dependencies).

Coverage is deliberately partial, per the gap-closure task's own scope-discipline instruction (fewer commands covered properly over more covered shallowly): IO group in full (all 11 command ids, request+reply, since that is where the recent live bug was -- BUS_SCAN (0x0B) added in a later pass, the bench incident cmd_ids.h's own comment documents), SYS group in full (all 8 command ids, request+reply, including the u32/u64 multi-byte fields and the REBOOT_BOOTLOADER magic-constant check), and one float-carrying command (TC_FORCE_TEMP) to pin f32 little-endian encoding end to end. MODEL/CT/RELAY/FAULT are enumerated and manually cross-checked in the task report but have no byte vectors here yet -- see that report's group/cmd agreement table.

sys._comment: SIMFW_TASK_ID_SYS, cmd_ids.h SIMFW_CMD_SYS_*. GET_VERSION/GET_CAPS reuse a synthetic version-block (protocol_version=7, min_compatible=5, fw 2.3.4, dirty=1, git_hash='abc1234') rather than real build-time constants, so this manifest is stable across firmware rebuilds -- it is testing write_version_block()'s/_decode_version_block()'s *shape*, not today's actual version string.

requests.name: set_timescale_10x
requests._note: payloads.py's SET_TIMESCALE takes a multiplier ('value'), not raw wire x100 -- 10.0x -> timescale_x100=1000

requests.name: set_seed_typical
requests._note: seed 0x12345678 -- proves byte-order, not just magnitude (all four bytes distinct). payloads.py's SET_SEED key is 'value'.

replies.name: get_caps_ok
replies._note: field names here match payloads.py's _sys_decode() dict keys exactly (tc_channel_count/ct_channel_count/relay_count, not the cmd_ids.h macro names)

replies.name: get_sim_state_typical
replies._note: seed 0xDEADBEEF and sim_time_us 0x0102030405060708 both have all-distinct bytes -- proves LE byte order for the u32 and the u64 field independently. Wire field is timescale_x100=250; payloads.py decodes it to a multiplier ('timescale': 2.5).

replies.name: reboot_bootloader_bad_args
replies._note: the only reply this command ever sends on the wire in practice, since the success path never ACKs at all (cmd_ids.h's own comment) -- this is the bad-magic/refusal path

replies.name: get_task_stats_two_tasks
replies._note: synthetic (not a real firmware capture) -- pins the per-record encoding [u8 task_stats_id, u16 allocated_bytes LE, u16 hwm_free_bytes LE], 5 bytes/record, and the [status, u8 task_count, records...] envelope (PROTOCOL.md sec 4 GET_TASK_STATS). task_stats_id 1/6 = SIMFW_TASK_STATS_ID_CMD_TASK/_TELEMETRY (cmd_ids.h). allocated=3072 (0x0C00 LE -> 00 0c), hwm_free=2500 (0x09C4 LE -> c4 09); allocated=4096 (0x1000 LE -> 00 10), hwm_free=1000 (0x03E8 LE -> e8 03). Only task_count is asserted here (not the full per-task list) -- decode_reply()'s per-task dicts carry additional PC-side-derived keys (peak_used_bytes/margin, PROTOCOL.md sec 4: 'the firmware reports the two raw numbers, never a derived ratio') that this test file's nested-equality check would otherwise reject; the full per-record decode (task_stats_id/allocated_bytes/hwm_free_bytes for BOTH records) is exercised byte-for-byte instead by tools/PcTools/tests/test_kilnsim_task_stats.py's test_decode_two_tasks against this exact hex string, and by firmware/SimFW/test/test_cmd_payload_vectors.c's own mirror of the encode side.

io._comment: SIMFW_TASK_ID_IO, cmd_ids.h SIMFW_CMD_IO_*. exp is i2c_owner_expander_t (0=EXP_1, 1=EXP_2 per cmd_task.c's `exp > I2C_OWNER_EXP_2` bound, i.e. valid range 0..2 -- vectors below stay in-range since these are wire-shape vectors, not owner-API range vectors).

replies.name: bus_scan_match
replies._note: configured 0x25/0x26 (decimal 37/38, this pass's bench-confirmed addresses), both found -- bitmap bit 29 (addr 0x25) and bit 30 (addr 0x26) set, i.e. byte index 3 (bits 24..31) = 0x60. bit n = address (0x08+n); bit 29 -> byte 29//8=3, bit 29%8=5 -> 0x20; bit 30 -> byte 3, bit 6 -> 0x40; 0x20|0x40=0x60.

replies.name: bus_scan_mismatch
replies._note: the exact bench incident this command exists to catch: firmware configured for the POR-default 0x20/0x21 (decimal 32/33), but only 0x25/0x26 actually ACK -- same found_bitmap as bus_scan_match, different configured_addr1/2, so match must be false.

tc_float_sample._comment: SIMFW_TASK_ID_TC, SIMFW_CMD_TC_FORCE_TEMP (cmd 2) only -- a single-f32-field command picked to pin little-endian IEEE-754 encoding end to end (PROTOCOL.md sec 5.2), independent of the all-integer IO/SYS coverage above. Not full TC group coverage -- see the task report's group/cmd table for what else was manually cross-checked but has no byte vector yet.
